title: RBAC Audit Stream Testbench and SIEM Export Matrix
body:
Overview:
This doc defines a lightweight testbench and validation matrix for the RBAC-driven audit stream and downstream SIEM exports. Purpose is to provide an automated, reproducible way to exercise RBAC v2 event flows (role grants/revokes, policy decisions, token issuance, delegation) through collector adapters and SIEM exporters, assert schema conformance, and verify control evidence workflows (generation, signing, retention, and replay).

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable test harness that can generate synthetic RBAC events and run them through our collector stack (edge agent -> ingest proxy -> normalizer -> exporter).
- Exercise edge cases: burst replays, out-of-order events, partial failures, and cross-region routing/fallbacks.
- Validate audit schema mapping for top SIEM targets (Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Elastic/Opensearch ingest, S3/GCS archival format).
- Check tamper-evidence properties (deterministic event IDs, cryptographic signatures, integrity headers) and proof-of-possession markers used by control evidence workflows.
- Produce a per-run export matrix summarizing conformance, latency, and loss rates.

Scope:
- Included: RBAC change events (role.create, role.update, role.delete, binding.create/delete), auth decisions (allow/deny), session lifecycle (issue, refresh, revoke), and policy-eval traces.
- Excluded: full application-level business events (outside RBAC/authorization domain), and PII-heavy payloads (do not include user PII in synthetic generator).

Testbench architecture (components):
1) Synthetic Event Generator (SEG): lightweight Go service that reads scenario manifests and emits event streams with configurable timestamps, sequence numbers, and optional intentional corruptions (missing fields, altered signatures).
- Modes: steady-state, burst, slow-drip, reordered
- Config knobs: events/sec, max-sequence-gap, clock-drift-ms, corrupt-rate-percent

2) Ingest Proxy (test harness instance): mirrors the production ingest proxy but with test-only toggles for response delay injection, auth failures, and backpressure behavior.

3) Collector Normalizer (local test container): applies the audit schema normalization mapping and attaches provenance envelope headers. Built to load mapping files dynamically so tests can validate multiple schema versions.

4) Export Adapters (pluggable):
- Splunk HEC adapter: validates HEC event JSON shape and token handling.
- Elastic bulk API adapter: validates bulk payload, index routing, and mapping fields.
- Archive adapter (S3/GCS Parquet/NDJSON): verifies field-level retention tags are present and that objects are partitioned by date/region.
- SIEM syslog/CEF shim: converts normalized events into CEF/syslog and ensures required fields map correctly.

5) Verification Runner: collects exporter receipts, compares arrivals to sent event log, and runs schema checks and cryptographic verification. Produces per-test-run report and export matrix (CSV + JSON summary).

Event schema and validation heuristics (high level):
- Core required fields: event_id, generated_at, source_service, event_type, actor_id, actor_type, target_resource, action, decision, sequence_num, signature, provenance_chain
- Deterministic ID rule: event_id = sha256(namespace || sequence_num || canonical_payload) to support replay detection in downstream systems.
- Signature rule: events must carry an ed25519 signature header populated by the edge signer; verification steps assert signer key id exists in the known-keys table and signature timestamp within +/- 5s of generated_at unless clock-drift mode used.
- Provenance chain: list of hop-ids (opaque strings) used to assert routing path; tests ensure chain length increments as events traverse test proxies.

Validation checks (examples):
- Schema conformance: producer-submitted event must match normalized schema; missing required fields -> fail.
- Idempotency and replay handling: duplicate sequence_num within same namespace should be rejected or de-duped by collector; test injects duplicates and asserts exactly-one delivery semantics to exporter (or explicit duplication flag).
- Reordering tolerance: simulate network reorders and assert sequence reassembly window behavior.
- Partial failure and retry: drop exporter ack randomly and ensure retry/backoff policy results in eventual delivery within SLO.
- Export adapter field mapping: fields present in normalized payload must map to expected SIEM fields (mapping matrix exercised).

SIEM Export Matrix (per-run summary format):
Each run emits a CSV/JSON matrix with rows for each exporter and columns: exporter_name, schema_version, total_sent, total_accepted, total_rejected, avg_write_latency_ms, max_write_latency_ms, schema_mismatch_count, signature_failures, partitioning_ok (yes/no), provenance_chain_ok (yes/no), sample_event_id.

Sample matrix (text):
- exporter_name: splunk-hec
  schema_version: v2.1
  total_sent: 8500
  total_accepted: 8496
  total_rejected: 4
  avg_write_latency_ms: 120
  max_write_latency_ms: 2200
  schema_mismatch_count: 2
  signature_failures: 1
  partitioning_ok: yes
  provenance_chain_ok: yes
  sample_event_id: 1b4f7e...

Test scenarios (recommended):
- S1: Baseline steady-state (1k eps for 10m) — expect zero schema mismatches, <0.1% rejected, avg latency <150ms.
- S2: Burst handling (10k eps burst for 30s) — assert backpressure behavior and safe fallback to secondary exporter.
- S3: Out-of-order replay (send sequences 1..100 with random reorder) — verify collector sequence reassembly window holds.
- S4: Corrupted-signature injection (0.5% events) — ensure signature failures are logged and routed to quarantine path; do not accept into archive.
- S5: Schema drift test (inject v2.0 and v2.1 events concurrently) — confirm normalizer applies correct mapping and annotates original schema_version.

Control evidence workflow integration points:
- Evidence manifest generation: testbench ensures each curator action produces a manifest entry with references to the archived object (s3://) and the corresponding event_id.
- Retention tagging: archive objects must include retention_policy and control_tags fields for downstream legal hold logic.
- Access audits: when RBAC role changes are exercised by the generator, verify that access-audit artifacts (who changed what and when) are present in both SIEM index and archive with matching event_id and signature.
- Attestation replay: provide a mode where the SEG replays a historical sequence (by event_id) and asserts the provenance_chain leads to the same signer; useful for runbook-driven forensics.

Operational runbook (short):
- Start testbench: ./bin/seg --scenario baseline --out ingest-proxy:9200
- Monitor: use /debug/metrics on normalizer and exporters; expect metrics: audit_events_in_total, audit_events_out_total, audit_schema_errors_total, audit_signature_failures_total
- If schema_mismatch_count > 0: capture first 10 mismatches with payload and normalized result and open SEC ticket with label audit-schema-failure.
- If signature_failures > 0: check key rotation list and edge-signer logs; do not delete failing events until triage complete.
- Emergency stop: set ingest-proxy to reject-new to drain and stop any further archival writes.

Metrics and acceptance criteria (per test run):
- Schema conformance >= 99.9%
- Signature verification pass rate >= 99.95% (except when intentional corruptions injected)
- Delivery success to primary exporter >= 99.5% under steady-state
- Archive objects presence >= 100% for non-quarantined events
- Testbench produces matrix and artifacts within 5 minutes of test end

Rollbacks, triage and incident notes:
- If exporter regression detected (sustained increase in schema_mismatch_count or avg_write_latency): revert collector-normalizer mapping to previous stable mapping (tagged in git), re-run the failing scenario in replay mode, and validate whether mapping change introduced the regression.
- For signature failures: check signer key revocation and clock skew incidents; escalate to cryptography team if root key compromised.

Appendix: sample synthetic event (canonicalized form used in test assertions)
{
  "event_id": "sha256:1b4f7e...",
  "generated_at": "2025-01-14T13:22:07Z",
  "source_service": "auth-edge-v2",
  "event_type": "role.binding.create",
  "actor_id": "svc:admin-console",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "target_resource": "org:acme-team:role:billing_admin",
  "action": "bind",
  "decision": "allow",
  "sequence_num": "00000000000000042",
  "signature": "ed25519:kt1...",
  "provenance_chain": ["edge-1", "proxy-3"]
}

Notes and next steps:
- Add CI job that runs the testbench against the staging ingest-proxy nightly and fails the pipeline on regressions in the export matrix thresholds.
- Expand exporter adapters to include vendor-specific field mappings for QRadar and Sumo Logic; collect sample mappings from security ops.
- Align retention tags with legal/compliance policy document (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).

Contact: Sana Patel (security-infra) — for questions or help running the harness.
